Mixpanel's breach disclosure was widely criticized as vague and poorly written, not disclosing what systems were accessed, what data was exposed, or the scale, in contrast to OpenAI's more detailed notice about the same incident.

OpenAI: 'On November 9, 2025, Mixpanel became aware of an attacker that gained unauthorized access to part of their systems and exported a dataset containing limited customer identifiable information and analytics information.'
After reviewing the Mixpanel security incident, 'OpenAI has terminated its use of Mixpanel' as a vendor, citing accountability for the highest bar of security and privacy.
Mixpanel performed global password resets for all employees following the smishing (SMS phishing) attack that led to unauthorized data export, suggesting employee credentials were compromised.
Ex-Mixpanel employee and current customer: 'I wish Mixpanel wasn't this expensive for a few 1000 users. But like any company in an economic market, they'll charge for what customers will bear.'
User dropped Mixpanel after free startup package expired because it would have cost '$x,000 per month' and they weren't getting enough value from it despite wanting funnels and user journey tracking.

'Mixpanel has the most obscure pricing model of any SAAS i've ever tried to integrate with... When we upgraded from their free tier to a paid tier we were DOWNGRADED from 20M events a month to 10K events a month.'
To match the free tier's 20M events on a paid plan would cost '$2,289 USD / month'; user cancelled paid plan and reverted to free tier, then searched for alternatives.
Group-level/account-level analytics useful for B2B SaaS is 'tucked away on one of Mixpanel's higher price plans,' limiting access for smaller customers.
A company reported spending $240K/year on Mixpanel, prompting them to build a replacement using BigQuery and Kubernetes to save money at scale.
Commenter's caution: 'Beware of thinking you can do this for $X,000/year on your own... Mixpanel does a LOT more than this tool... there's a reason Mixpanel has so many engineers.'

'Getting a front end anywhere near as slick and powerful as Mixpanel's is an even bigger challenge than the data pipeline... I've seen PMs spend hours in mixpanel quickly generating custom report after custom report.'

Complaint about vendor lock-in: 'The tool is lovely, their export policy is great, but there's something about actually owning your data' — users often end up re-exporting Mixpanel data to their own warehouse anyway.

Tip for controlling costs: 'The easy and cheap way to keep mixpanel cost under control is sample events or send only unique events per session.' Another user reported saving 60% by limiting event frequency per user.

On Mixpanel's Flow feature: 'This is the coolest thing I have seen in Analytics for a long time. This really gets to the heart of most of the information you need on user flows and its fast and clear.'
Paying Mixpanel customer feedback on Flow: 'My biggest request is the same as the biggest request for the rest of Mixpanel: remove the wall between page views and other events.'

Usability complaints about Flow's hover-based UI: 'Requires too much effort (rolling over hover states) to dig out information' and is 'Very difficult to use on iPad... hard to hit the red part of the circle.'
Mixpanel rewrote their event-ingestion server from Erlang to Python after two years, citing that 'the code has become difficult to maintain. No one on our team is an Erlang expert.'

A Mixpanel team member responded to criticism explaining the original Erlang server was 'one of the very first things written when we started Mixpanel over 2 years ago' and had barely been touched despite scaling from 0 to thousands of requests per second.
